questions.question: The photoelectric effect is the process whereby:
options: Electrons are ejected from a metal surface by light of suitable frequency
Electrons orbit faster in bright light

questions.question: Light BELOW a metal's threshold frequency:
options: Ejects electrons only if very bright
Ejects no electrons at all, regardless of brightness or exposure time

questions.question: The energy of a single photon is given by:
The work function of a metal is:
options: The maximum kinetic energy of an ejected electron
The minimum energy needed to eject an electron from that metal's surface, W₀ = hf₀
The energy of the brightest photon
The same value for all metals

questions.question: The photoelectric equation states that the photon's energy is:
options: E = W₀ + E k max — exit cost plus the electron's maximum kinetic energy

questions.question: Light of wavelength 400 nm has a frequency of:
That 400 nm light (photon energy 4,97 × 10⁻¹⁹ J) strikes sodium, W₀ = 3,65 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. The maximum kinetic energy of an ejected electron is:
The kinetic energy in the equation is called the MAXIMUM because:
options: It is measured at the peak of the wave
It belongs to electrons ejected from the very surface; deeper electrons pay extra to escape and emerge slower
The equation rounds all answers up

questions.question: Increasing the intensity of light ABOVE the threshold frequency causes:
options: Faster electrons with the same photocurrent
More electrons ejected per second, each with unchanged maximum kinetic energy

questions.question: Increasing the frequency of the light (photon arrival rate unchanged) causes:
options: Greater maximum kinetic energy per electron, with no rise in the number ejected per second
More electrons per second at the same speed

questions.question: Below the threshold, making the light brighter achieves nothing because:
options: The photons cancel each other out
Bright light heats the metal too much
No electron can pool the energy of two photons — each weak photon fails individually

questions.question: Which observed fact does the WAVE model of light fail to explain?
options: Instant emission in faint light, a sharp frequency threshold, and kinetic energy that ignores brightness

questions.question: An atom emits a photon when an electron:
options: Jumps to a higher energy level
Drops from a higher energy level to a lower one, the photon carrying exactly the energy difference

questions.question: An atomic emission spectrum appears as:
options: Bright, sharp coloured lines on a black background

questions.question: An absorption spectrum shows dark lines at:
options: Only the red end of the spectrum
Exactly the frequencies where the same element's hot gas would emit

questions.question: Sharp spectral lines are direct evidence that:
options: Atomic energy levels are quantised — electrons cannot hold in-between energies
All elements share the same energy ladder

subtopics.title: The Bouncer at the Metal's Door

questions.question: In the club picture, the bouncer's fixed exit fee represents:
options: The work function of the metal

questions.question: The house rule 'no whip-rounds, no pooling' captures the physics that:
options: One photon deals with one electron — energies of separate photons cannot combine
The metal absorbs all light equally

questions.question: Dim light above the threshold frequency ejects electrons:
options: Immediately — the first rich-enough photon pays in full; dimness only means fewer ejections per second
Only if the metal is heated

subtopics.title: Ten Soft Throws Never Beat One Hard Throw

questions.question: The crucial rule of the strength-machine picture is that the machine:
options: Resets completely between swings — nothing accumulates

questions.question: In the analogy, swings per minute and the force of one swing represent respectively:
options: Intensity (photons per second) and frequency (energy per photon)

questions.question: Striking harder than the minimum makes the slider fly past the bell. The surplus represents:
The classic error this analogy prevents is writing that:
options: Brighter light makes each ejected electron faster
The threshold depends on the metal

questions.question: The old orange streetlights display the signature of:
Spectra show sharp lines rather than a smear because:
options: Electrons occupy fixed rungs on an energy ladder — fixed drops give fixed photon energies and pure colours
The gas is too thin to glow fully
Hot atoms move too fast to blur

questions.question: A cool gas in front of a rainbow source produces dark lines because its atoms:
options: Absorb exactly the photons matching upward jumps on their ladder

questions.question: Helium's presence in the Sun was discovered by:
options: Reading its signature lines in sunlight before the element was found on Earth
Comparing the Sun's colour with sodium lamps
